notes: Independently checked source identity: canonical text is the PMC full author manuscript of Sleep Preferentially Enhances Memory for Emotional Components of Scenes, by Jessica D Payne, Robert Stickgold, Kelley Swanberg, and Elizabeth A Kensinger. Publication line Psychol Sci. 2008 Aug;19(8):781–788 and DOI 10.1111/j.1467-9280.2008.02157.x match the neutral original reference. Includes Method, Results, Discussion, and references, not merely an abstract. No PDF supplied; section locators used. Only assigned unfinished fields assessed; other fields are placeholders. Background-specific Valence × Delay interaction identified by outcome, sleep/wake comparison, and valence factors. Only p > .10 is printed for this test; no effect size or F statistic is given. Nearby partial eta-squared/F values belong to full-model interactions or the negative-object comparison and cannot be assigned to this background-specific test. The descriptive statement that memory for backgrounds was unchanged by sleep (38% vs. 38%) is not a printed interaction effect size. Other Analyses reports corrected full-model interactions, not a background-specific effect statistic. No conversion performed; unassigned p remains a placeholder.
